raw_response:
The test is non-circular in construction, but it is not automatically non-trivial. The critical worry is real: once you restrict to synonymous-family zero-sum contrasts, you have already removed the amino-acid means and much of the low-frequency content. A high  $E_3$  fraction may be generic for this carrier. So the raw statement

$$\rho_3(q)=\frac{\|P_{E_3}q\|^2}{\|q\|^2}\ \text{is high}$$

means almost nothing unless compared against a very tight synonymous-zero-sum null.
The right baseline is not random vectors in  $\mathbb R^{64}$ . It is not even random 61-sense vectors. It is the full synonymous residual space

$$W_{\rm syn}
=
\{x:\sum_{c\in F_a}x_c=0\text{ for every amino-acid family }F_a,\ x_{\rm stop}=0\}.$$

The first diagnostic must be:

$$\bar\rho_{3,\rm syn}
=
\frac{\operatorname{tr}(P_{W_{\rm syn}}P_{E_3})}{\dim W_{\rm syn}}.$$

If  $\bar\rho_{3,\rm syn}$  is already large, then B $^*_{Q6}$  being  $E_3$ -heavy is mostly a theorem about synonymous residualization, not a bridge. In that case the matched null swamps the result.
So the honest answer to (1) is:
The test is non-circular only because B $^*_{Q6}$  was defined without q6/Foldbin/Zeckendorf labels and  $E_3$  was defined independently by the chemical-character Hamming scheme. But it is non-trivial only if B $^*_{Q6}$  beats a null inside the synonymous residual space with the same family-support and contrast-profile constraints. Raw  $E_3$  concentration is not enough.
The sharpest statistic is not per-vector  $\rho_3$  and not the mean of the nine displayed basis vectors. Those are basis-dependent. A different orthogonalization of the same biological subspace could change the individual  $\rho_3$  values while leaving the structural content unchanged.
The invariant statistic should be the projector trace between the B $^*_{Q6}$  subspace and  $E_3$ :

$$\tau(B,E_3)
=
\operatorname{tr}(P_B P_{E_3})
=
\sum_{i=1}^{9}\cos^2\theta_i,$$

where  $B=\operatorname{span}(B^*_{Q6})$ ,  $P_B$  is the orthogonal projector onto that 9-dimensional span, and  $\theta_i$  are the principal angles between  $B$  and  $E_3$ .
Normalize it as

$$\bar\tau(B,E_3)=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{tr}(P_B P_{E_3}).$$

That is the correct primary statistic. The principal-angle spectrum is the diagnostic: it tells you whether the signal is broad across the 9-dimensional subspace or driven by one lucky axis. Per-vector  $\rho_3$  should be reported only as an audit table, not as the result.
The pre-registered null should be a hierarchy, with the strongest one deciding the claim:


Synonymous residual Grassmann null.
Random 9-dimensional subspaces  $B'\subset W_{\rm syn}$ . This tests whether B $^*$  is special beyond generic synonymous residualization.


Family-dimension matched null.
Random subspaces built with the same number of contrast degrees contributed by 2-fold, 3-fold, 4-fold, and 6-fold amino-acid families. This prevents “large families naturally touch  $E_3$ ” from becoming the signal.


Template-matched null.
Random contrast systems with the same coefficient templates as the observed axes: 1-vs-1, 1-vs-2, 2-vs-4, 4-vs-2, purine-vs-pyrimidine within a family, and first-minus-last style contrasts, but assigned to admissible synonymous families without using q6 labels or the reassignment set  $R$ .


Support-profile matched null.
Preserve the observed family supports and contrast sparsity profile as much as possible, but randomize the actual zero-sum directions within those supports.


The test is only interesting if B $^*$  beats all four. If it only beats the loose nulls, it is coincidence or a generic property of synonymous residualization.
On (3): selecting exactly the  $>2$ -fold degenerate families is not q6-circular by itself, because it is defined from the genetic code’s degeneracy table, not from  $E_3$ , q6, Foldbin, or Zeckendorf. But it is still dangerous. It can be post-selection circularity if the set of families or axes was chosen because they are the ones whose support union matches the 13 reassigned codons or because they looked spectrally interesting.
The clean distinction is:


If the rule was fixed as “take a canonical residual basis for all synonymous families with internal degeneracy beyond a trivial 2-codon pair, plus a separately justified 2-codon stress contrast,” then it is not q6-circular.


If the rule was “take the contrasts whose union is exactly the known 13 lability codons,” then it is not q6-circular but it is R-circular.


If the rule was adjusted after seeing  $E_3$  concentration, then the test is invalid as certification.


Also, be careful: B $^*_{Q6}$  as listed is not purely “ $>2$ -fold families,” because K $_{AAA}$  is a 2-codon Lys contrast, and the global f3-stress vector spans many families. That does not make it invalid, but it means the null must match the actual recipe, not a simplified story about  $>2$ -fold degeneracy.
On (4), the only outcome that could justify certified structural forcing is very strong:

$$\bar\tau(B,E_3)$$

must be near the algebraic maximum, or exactly maximal, under the tightest template/support-matched synonymous-zero-sum null, with a principal-angle spectrum showing broad alignment rather than one dominant vector. Ideally:

$$\operatorname{tr}(P_B P_{E_3}) \approx 9,$$

meaning the entire 9-dimensional B $^*$  subspace lies almost inside  $E_3$ , and the null distribution places that in an exact or effectively unreachable tail.
Even then, the wording should be precise:
certified structural forcing of the B $^*_{Q6}$  codon-spelling residual basis into the canonical  $E_3$  spectral layer.
Not yet:
certified biological mechanism.
For the latter, the cross-organism  $d_{\rm resid4}$  gate still matters. Since the reported cross-organism data are non-resolving and measured tRNA-tAI/TE absorb almost none of the residual, the structural test can certify alignment of two codon-intrinsic objects, but it cannot certify selection, translation, or expression-level causality.
The result should be called coincidence if any of the following happens:


 $\bar\tau(B,E_3)$  is typical under random 9-subspaces of  $W_{\rm syn}$ ;


the signal disappears under family-dimension or template-matched nulls;


the alignment is driven by one or two axes rather than the subspace;


the support union  $R=13$  is necessary to get significance;


f3-stress or another broad composition-like vector carries the trace;


the outcome is statistically significant but not algebraically extreme.


If the test is vacuous, the non-vacuous alternative is not another structural spectral statistic. It is the held-out biological gate:

$$\text{Does the exported }d_{\rm resid4}\text{ organism matrix have a reproducible projection onto }E_3$$

after organism holdout, amino-acid residualization, tRNA/tAI/TE controls, and sign/permutation stability? That is the only route that turns the  $E_3$  structural layer into a biological axis rather than an elegant codon-spelling fact.
My brutally honest verdict:
Run the projector-trace test, but treat it as a falsification check for vacuity, not as a likely forcing certificate. The null probably has a high  $E_3$  baseline because synonymous zero-sum contrasts already suppress  $E_0/E_1$ . The test becomes meaningful only if B $^*$  is almost entirely inside  $E_3$  and remains extreme under template/support-matched nulls.
The sharpest next question is:
Is  $\operatorname{tr}(P_{B^*}P_{E_3})/9$  still extreme after conditioning on the full synonymous-zero-sum carrier, family-dimension profile, coefficient templates, and support sparsity, or is the apparent  $E_3$  concentration just the generic spectrum of amino-acid-residual codon contrasts?
